app.title: MetaboSpatial-CCI
app.summary: A person loads a spatial transcriptomics dataset, either seeded demo data or an uploaded file, picks a version of the reference database, and sets the quality-control, diffusion-solver and statistics parameters in a sidebar. They run the pipeline. It filters and normalises the spots, infers how much each spot secretes from enzyme expression, models how each metabolite diffuses across the tissue, scores metabolite-receptor pairs and tests them by permutation, and aggregates the results into a cell-type communication network. They then go through tabs: an overview of counts and top hits, paired spatial maps for one chosen metabolite, a ranked table and chart of every pair marked by significance, and a sender-receiver network heatmap. At the end they download the interaction and hub tables as CSV.

task.text: Infer and rank spatially resolved, statistically tested signalling interactions from expression data on a tissue section, and summarise them as a sender-receiver network between cell types.

data.text: A spatial expression matrix of spots by genes, with x-y coordinates for each spot, scored against a curated reference database that links each signalling molecule to its receptors, synthesis and degradation enzymes and transporters.
data.item: a measured spot on a tissue section, with coordinates and gene expression counts

stage.text: analysing spatial expression data after it is collected, to infer and rank signalling interactions

mechanism.text: Sidebar parameters feed one cached pipeline run, triggered by a button. Its results fill tabbed views: summary metrics with top-ranked tables, two spatial scatter maps side by side for a metabolite chosen from a dropdown, a sortable table of all pairs with a bar chart coloured by significance, and a sender-by-receiver heatmap with paired bars. A final tab exports the tables as CSV.

field.text: cell-cell communication inference with reaction-diffusion modelling on spatial transcriptomics, in biology

workflow.name: run a parameterised analysis pipeline over a dataset and export ranked, significance-tested results

steps.here: A radio button picks seeded demo data or an uploaded file with spatial coordinates. A dropdown picks which version of the reference database to score against. The status metric shows Ready or Waiting for data.

steps.step: set the analysis parameters and compute a value from the data
steps.here: Sliders set minimum genes and counts per spot, the normalisation target, pixel size and the number of permutations. Dropdowns pick an FFT or finite-difference diffusion solver and an NNLS or mean-score deconvolution. Run Analysis then runs QC, secretion inference, diffusion, receptor scoring, a permutation test with Moran's I, deconvolution and network building.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The Overview tab shows counts of spots, genes, metabolites and interactions, the top 10 metabolite-receptor pairs with p-values and significance stars, and the top hub cell types.
In the Metabolites tab a dropdown picks one metabolite. Two maps side by side show its net secretion or uptake per spot and its predicted diffused concentration, each with mean, maximum and minimum.

steps.step: rank all items and flag the significant ones
steps.here: The Interactions tab lists every pair with mean score, z-score, p-value, Moran's I and a yes/no significance flag, sorted by score, with counts of the total and the significant. A horizontal bar chart of the top 15 colours significant pairs red.

steps.step: summarise the items as a network between groups
steps.here: The CCI Network tab draws a sender-by-receiver heatmap of communication strength between cell types, with paired bars of each type's sender and receiver strength.
The Download tab saves the full interaction table and the hub cell-type table as CSV files.

distinctive: Spatial spread is modelled physically: a steady-state reaction-diffusion equation turns the secretion at each spot into a concentration field, with a choice between an FFT and a finite-difference solver.
Secretion is inferred from synthesis enzymes minus degradation enzymes, using a curated database that the person can switch between versions.
Each metabolite-receptor pair is tested for significance by spatial permutation against Moran's I, and the significance is carried through the tables and the colours of the chart.
Spots are deconvolved into cell-type proportions so that interactions at the spot level roll up into a sender-receiver network with hub detection.
For each metabolite, the secretion map and the diffused-concentration map are shown side by side.

parts.title: Parameters sidebar
parts.summary: Collects the database choice, QC, diffusion and statistics settings, and runs the cached pipeline when Run Analysis is pressed.

parts.title: Data input
parts.summary: Lets the person choose seeded demo data on a hexagonal grid of spots, or upload their own file with spatial coordinates.

parts.title: Analysis overview
parts.summary: Shows dataset and interaction counts, the top 10 metabolite-receptor pairs with p-values and significance stars, and the top hub cell types.

parts.title: Metabolite secretion and concentration maps
parts.summary: For a metabolite picked from a dropdown, maps its net secretion and its predicted diffused concentration across the tissue side by side, each with summary values.

parts.title: Metabolite-receptor interactions
parts.summary: Lists every pair ranked by mean score, with z-score, p-value, Moran's I and a significance flag, and charts the top 15 with significant pairs in red.

parts.title: Cell-cell communication network
parts.summary: Shows communication strength from sender to receiver cell types as a heatmap, with each type's sender and receiver strength as paired bars.

parts.title: Download results
parts.summary: Exports the full interaction table and the hub cell-type table as CSV files.
